name: Crisp chicken thighs over garlicky white beans, chard, and satsuma
intro: Bone-in thighs in the air fryer, skin-side up, until the skin crackles and the meat is juicy, set over white beans simmered in a skillet with garlic, chard, stock, and satsuma. A spoonful of the chicken's drippings goes into the beans.
needs: 1 can white beans, drained and rinsed
½ bunch Swiss chard, stems chopped, leaves torn
Salt, black pepper, and chile flakes

steps.text: Pat the chicken completely dry, trim any skin hanging off the edges, and salt both sides. Dry skin is what crisps.
Set the thighs in the air fryer skin-side up, spaced apart in one layer. Cook until the skin is deep golden and crisp and the thickest thigh reads about 185°F. There's no need to flip them.
With 15 minutes to go, warm the oil in the 12-inch skillet over medium. Add the garlic, chard stems, and a pinch of chile flakes and cook until the stems soften.
Add the beans, stock, and satsuma juice and simmer, mashing a few beans against the pan so the liquid turns creamy.
Stir in the chard leaves until they wilt, and a spoonful of the drippings from under the chicken. Season with salt and pepper.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes. Beans and greens in shallow bowls, a thigh or two on top, satsuma zest, pickled fennel, and bread for the juices.

how_it_works: An air fryer is a small, powerful convection oven: hot air moving fast over the skin dries and renders it, and the fat drips away instead of pooling, so the skin crisps without a sear. Thighs are forgiving and are best around 185°F, where their connective tissue has melted. Beans simmered with stock and mashed a little make their own sauce, and the drippings give it the chicken's flavor.
swaps: Cauliflower florets in the beans, in place of the chard.
A lemon instead of the satsuma, for sharper beans.
French green lentils (cooked) instead of the beans.
leftovers: Pack a thigh over the beans for lunch. Recrisp the chicken in the air fryer at 375°F for 5 minutes and warm the beans in a small pan.

nutrition.serving: Half the recipe: two thighs over half the beans and chard, and a thick slice of sourdough.
